newsitem.title: EGYPT: Prominent Egyptian writer Moustafa Amin dies.
newsitem.headline: Prominent Egyptian writer Moustafa Amin dies.

text.p: Egyptian writer Moustafa Amin, a pioneer of Arab journalism whose career lasted over 60 years, died on Sunday, his colleagues said. He was 83.
He started writing for well-established magazines before becoming deputy chief editor of Akher Sa'a (Last Hour) magazine in 1934 and chief editor in 1939.
In 1944, Amin and his twin brother Ali founded Akhbar Al-Youm (Today's News) newspaper, and two other magazines two years later.
After nationalisation of the press in the early 1960s, Amin became chief editor of Dar al-Hilal, one of the largest publishing houses in Egypt.

Amin was convicted of spying for the United States and sent to prison under the late president Gamal Abdul Nasser. He was set free on health grounds after former president Anwar Sadat took power in 1970.
He continued writing his column "Fekra" (An Idea) for several Arab newspapers until his death. He also wrote novels that were turned into movies.
